title: Collecting wood core samples from Macassar ebony (Diospyros celebica Bakh.) for multi-purpose analysis using pickering punch
author: Siregar, Majiidu, et al.
materials: Dried wood cores are drilled by Dremel 3000 to obtain 50–100 mg powder then placed in a new 1.5- or 2 mL tube. Clean the Dremel by using 70% Alcohol before continuing to the next sample. Next step, add 2 mm 3–5 beads and a bit of sterile sand into each tube and grind with TissueLyser II from Qiagen at 25 Hz for 5 min. The genomic DNA can be extracted using modified CTAB method [6]. The CTAB buffer contains 10% CTAB, Tris–HCl, 5 M NaCl, 0.5 M EDTA, 1% PVP, β-Mercaptoethanol, and dH2O.

The samples may be used further for chemical analysis after the NIR. Weight the wood core as much as 500 mg . Samples are extracted with 5 ml of ethanol. Sonicate and filter the samples for 30 min with a 0.2-micrometer filter. Inject the sample into an instrument for liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).

steps.title: Extract wood core and store
steps.instruction: Assemble the extraction tools (5 lb and 10 lb sledge hammers, punch, end‑cap, slide‑hammer, metal rod, silica gel, petroleum jelly). Position the punch on the tree 50–70 cm above ground on the appropriate side, screw the end‑cap onto the punch until no threads are exposed, and tap lightly with the 5 lb hammer. Then knock the punch into the tree at a 90° angle and use the 10 lb hammer to drive it steadily to a depth of 12 cm. Unscrew the end‑cap, attach the slide‑hammer and tighten until threads are hidden, slide the hammer back against the stop point to pull the punch out, remove the wood core with the metal rod, and place the core in a 12 cm × 20 cm zip‑lock bag with silica gel for storage. Finally, cover the extraction hole with petroleum jelly to protect the tree.

substeps.instruction: Gather 5 lb and 10 lb sledge hammers, punch, end‑cap, slide‑hammer, metal rod, silica gel, petroleum jelly.
Measure 50–70 cm up the trunk and place the punch on the chosen side.
Screw end‑cap onto punch until no thread is exposed.
Tap punch with 5 lb hammer, then drive with 10 lb hammer at 90° angle to 12 cm depth.
Unscrew end‑cap, attach slide‑hammer, tighten fully.
Slide hammer back to stop point and extract punch.
Remove core with metal rod and store in zip‑lock bag with silica gel.
Seal extraction hole with petroleum jelly.

steps.title: Prepare DNA extraction sample
steps.instruction: Drill each dried wood core with a Dremel 3000 to obtain 50–100 mg of powder, place the powder in a clean 1.5 mL or 2 mL tube, clean the Dremel with 70 % alcohol before each core, add 3–5 beads (2 mm) and a small amount of sterile sand, then grind in a TissueLyser II (Qiagen) at 25 Hz for 5 min. Extract genomic DNA using a modified CTAB buffer containing 10 % CTAB, Tris‑HCl, 5 M NaCl, 0.5 M EDTA, 1 % PVP, β‑mercaptoethanol, and dH₂O.

substeps.instruction: Drill core to 50–100 mg powder with Dremel 3000.
Transfer powder to a new 1.5 mL or 2 mL tube.
Wipe Dremel tip with 70 % alcohol before next sample.
Add 3–5 × 2 mm beads and a pinch of sterile sand to the tube.
Grind at 25 Hz for 5 min using TissueLyser II.
Proceed with DNA extraction using CTAB buffer (10 % CTAB, Tris‑HCl, 5 M NaCl, 0.5 M EDTA, 1 % PVP, β‑mercaptoethanol, dH₂O).

steps.title: Prepare anatomical slide
steps.instruction: Boil the hardwood core for approximately 30 min, then cut cross‑, radial‑, and tangential‑sections with a sharp knife. Stain sections with safranin, dehydrate, mount on an object‑glass using Entellan, and cover with a cover glass to create a permanent slide for microscopic observation.

substeps.instruction: Boil the wood core for ~30 min.
Section the core in cross, radial, and tangential planes with a sharp knife.
Apply safranin stain to sections.
Dehydrate the stained sections.
Place sections on an object‑glass and mount with Entellan.
Cover with a cover glass to finalize the slide.

steps.title: Prepare NIR composite sample
steps.instruction: Combine 3–5 individual wood cores to form one composite (45 composites total), grind the composite to obtain 900–1500 mg of powder with a particle size of 40–60 mesh, and run the powder in the Near‑Infrared Spectroscopy instrument.

substeps.instruction: Select 3–5 cores and mix them into a single composite.
Grind the composite to 900–1500 mg powder, achieving 40–60 mesh size.
Load the powder into the NIR instrument for analysis.

steps.title: Prepare LC‑MS/MS chemical sample
steps.instruction: Weigh up to 500 mg of wood core material, extract with 5 mL ethanol, sonicate and filter the extract for 30 min using a 0.2 µm filter, then inject the filtered solution into the LC‑MS/MS system.

substeps.instruction: Weigh ≤500 mg of wood material.
Add 5 mL ethanol and mix.
Sonicate and filter the mixture for 30 min through a 0.2 µm filter.
Inject the filtrate into the LC‑MS/MS instrument.
